name: Hoping You'd Come
tagline: You make people feel expected. Very few people can.
epigraph: A captain wrote this toddy down from a barman said never to forget a face.
glassware: a small wineglass (about 250 ml), one plain lump of ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v3: ready. Barnum check sentence by sentence: no sentence says only "you like having people over"; every line is tied to preparation-as-hope or to being expected. Sibling echoes moved off in v3: "never say out loud is" (*Not Only the Way*) → "never tell them is"; "That's the part of him" (*Standing By*) → "That's where I see you in him"; "for us today" (lint: one bartender speaks) → "by today's taste". The he/him/his warnings in yours 1–4 are Willard and the captain, never the guest (accepted by Wren, round 6). History about 41% of the words. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/orsamus-willard.md`: *Oxford Companion to Spirits and Cocktails*, WILLARD, ORSAMUS (David Wondrich) pdf 2192–2194, CITY HOTEL pdf 469, TODDY pdf 2035, COCK-TAIL pdf 494; David Wondrich, *Imbibe!* pdf 20, 22, 76, 138–139, 171, 175; J. E. Alexander, *Transatlantic Sketches* (1833), vol. 2, p. 300, read on the page (archive.org `transatlanticsk01unkngoog`; first found through the Chanticleer Society transcription). Drink: Willard's Apple-toddy (Alexander p. 300), Jerry Thomas's hot Apple Toddy (1862, via *Imbibe!* pdf 139, set aside); *Flavor Matrix* apple pairings consulted and set aside (Tomás, round 2). Room notes: `work/lover-caregiver/`.
names_note: **Hoping You'd Come**, the room's pick (all three, round 6): the sentence this person never says, and the position. **Expected** was Tomás's pick in round 4; he withdrew it in round 5 because it repeats the tagline's "feel expected". Also considered: *The Fairest Apples* (the captain's page's words), *Ready for You*, *Kept Ready*, *Every Room Ready*. No "before", "door" or "calls" in any of them (sibling names and epigraphs).
open_items: **"A spoonful and a half" (y4), Tomás's optional note in round 7:** it could be read as tablespoons, and 1½ tablespoons would push the drink over the sugar ceiling; "a teaspoon and a half" matches the recipe's 1½ tsp exactly. It crossed with Wren's sign-off and wasn't answered in the room. The text is unchanged. Robin's call.

**The epigraph's "said never to forget a face":** Hester noted in round 7 that it could also read as an instruction, and offered "from a barman who, he said, never forgot a face". Wren kept v3's wording so that there's no bare "he" in a line read cold. Tomás's sign-off covers both.

**The dossier Resonance** (Wren's, round 6) still describes y4 as "the one person who wrote him down". The reading itself was corrected for A3 ("One of his guests did write his toddy down"). This is research-only text.

**His sugar is changed:** a fourth part of sugar reads OUT at 30.6 g/100 ml, so ours is 1½ tsp, owned in y4 and in the recipe note. "Far too sweet by today's taste" is our modern judgement, marked as ours. The fourths are unit-less on the page. Apple, brandy and water are 60 g / 60 ml / 60 ml.

**Edges:** a very sweet apple pushes the first sips about 0.5 g/100 ml over the sugar band. The `roasted_apple` ingredient values are unsourced (Tomás added them in round 4, safe-side, none of the five vetoes). The nutmeg is left off on purpose (it counts as `nuts`).

**Dates:** the books disagree (fact card C1). The reading dates nothing, and "until 1848" is the only date both agree on. The ten-year guest is told as one of the stories told of him (Oxford pdf 2193).
**For the Knight room (lover-hero):** the captain's 1833 Cocktail may be cited as the captain's record, never as Willard's (fact card C3).
